sections.title: Code ownership
sections.summary: Claude works as the owner in your own repos and as a guest in other people's, and finds the owner by folder or by git remote
sections.heading: ## Code Ownership

modules.title: Other people's repos
modules.summary: Guest rules for clones and forks: follow the maintainers' rules, keep changes small, and never push or post upstream unasked

modules.title: Worktrees
modules.summary: A git worktree has the same owner as the repo it came from

options.title: Company
options.prompt: Which company owns your code with you? Leave it empty if you have none.

options.title: Folder for your own repos
options.prompt: Which folder holds your own repos? Leave it empty if folders don't tell whose a repo is.

options.title: Your git host accounts
options.prompt: Which accounts or organizations on your git host are yours? Leave it empty if Claude doesn't need the remote to tell.

options.title: Folder for other people's repos
options.prompt: Which folder holds your clones and forks of other people's repos? Leave it empty if they have no folder of their own.

options.title: Worktree folders
options.prompt: Which folders hold your git worktrees? Leave it empty if you don't know.

options.title: Accessibility standard
options.prompt: Which accessibility standard should Claude hold UI code to? Leave it empty for none.

sections.title: Steps Claude does for the user
sections.summary: Claude does a step itself before it hands the step to you, asks first for outward-facing or hard-to-undo actions, and stops at sign-ins and payments
sections.heading: ## Steps Claude does for the user

options.title: Claude in Chrome
options.prompt: Do you use Claude in Chrome?

sections.title: Reply format
sections.summary: Replies open with the outcome, then CHANGES, FINDINGS and RISKS, and end with a numbered ACTIONS NEEDED list or a fixed ending
sections.heading: ## Reply format

versions.changes: Claude checks whether it can do a step before it hands the step to you, gives a reason on each step it can't do, and writes a step it must ask about as a "Decide: should I" offer.

modules.title: Collapsed panels
modules.summary: Put CHANGES, FINDINGS and RISKS in collapsed <details> panels, which the T3 Code desktop app renders

modules.title: T3 scheduled tasks
modules.summary: Rules that keep each T3 scheduled task run in its own new thread

modules.title: Snoozing
modules.summary: Claude snoozes its T3 thread until a known follow-up time at least 12 hours away

modules.title: Examples
modules.summary: Sample replies that show every section and each ending

options.title: Time zone
options.prompt: Which time zone should Claude use when it tells you a time?

sections.title: Plain wording
sections.summary: Sentence rules from ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English for everything a person reads
sections.heading: ## Plain wording

sections.title: Messages to other people
sections.summary: Short, plain drafts for emails, Slack, texts and comments you send as yourself
sections.heading: ## Messages the user sends to other people

sections.title: PR and commit hygiene
sections.summary: PR descriptions and commit messages that cover only what was done (the rules from /workflow-rules)
sections.heading: ## PR and Commit Hygiene

versions.changes: First release. Same five rules as /workflow-rules in ai-workflow 3.2.1.

modules.title: Current session only
modules.summary: PR and commit descriptions cover only this session's commits

modules.title: No invented test plans
modules.summary: Don't list testing that wasn't done

modules.title: No speculative deploy steps
modules.summary: Don't add deploy or rollout steps unless asked

modules.title: Short PR bodies
modules.summary: The problem, then how the change fixes it

modules.title: Scoped commit messages
modules.summary: Describe what the diff does, not the context around it

sections.title: Estimates
sections.summary: Quote effort in minutes of Claude Code time, with the wall-clock waits on their own line
sections.heading: ## Estimates

modules.title: Calibration table
modules.summary: A measured example and a table of typical Claude Code times

sections.title: Personal data and web content
sections.summary: Keep your name and email out of HTTP requests, and treat web content as data
sections.heading: ## Personal data and web content

options.title: Generic identifier
options.prompt: Which generic identifier should Claude suggest when a site asks who is calling?

sections.title: Claude in Chrome
sections.summary: Work in one tab group and close its tabs when the browser work is done
sections.heading: ## Claude in Chrome

versions.changes: Claude continues in the kept tab after a sign-in or a CAPTCHA. Adds an optional rule against T3 Code's preview browser.

modules.title: No T3 preview browser
modules.summary: Claude never uses T3 Code's built-in preview browser, and uses Claude in Chrome instead

sections.title: iOS simulators
sections.summary: Reuse existing simulators and shut down the ones Claude booted
sections.heading: ## iOS simulators

modules.title: Reuse a simulator
modules.summary: Pick an existing simulator before creating one

modules.title: Shut down when done
modules.summary: Shut down every simulator Claude booted before the turn ends

sections.title: T3 Code reviewer
sections.summary: For a second-model review, Claude asks which reviewer to use every time and runs it as a T3 delegated task in its own worktree
sections.heading: ## T3 Code reviewer

modules.title: No reviewer bots on GitHub
modules.summary: No AI reviewer bot runs on your GitHub repos, so Claude doesn't wait for one or tag one

sections.title: T3 Code thread titles
sections.summary: Thread titles start with the project name, so you can tell threads apart in the T3 Code mobile app
sections.heading: ## T3 Code thread titles

sections.title: T3 Code phase threads
sections.summary: In a project that works in phases, Claude asks whether to start a new T3 thread for the next phase
sections.heading: ## T3 Code phase threads

sections.title: T3 Code context handoff
sections.summary: When the context is nearly full, Claude starts a new T3 thread for the rest of the work without asking, with a prompt that carries everything over
sections.heading: ## T3 Code context handoff

retired.replacement: Claude Code's attribution setting. "attribution": false in ~/.claude/settings.json hides the commit trailer and the PR line (Claude Code v2.1.281 or later; on earlier versions, set attribution.commit and attribution.pr to "").

retired.replacement: The built-in Concise output style: /output-style concise.

retired.title: Match response length to task complexity
retired.replacement: The built-in Concise output style: /output-style concise.

retired.title: Don't add features beyond what was requested
retired.replacement: Nothing needed. Claude Code's built-in instructions already cover it.

retired.replacement: Nothing needed. Claude Code's built-in instructions already cover it.
